subject: Cloud Computing
title: Storage Options in IaaS
description: A 60-second lesson on Storage Options in IaaS.

hook.text: Your server needs storage. IaaS gives you three types: block, object, and file. Choose wisely.

buildup.text: Block storage (EBS) acts like a hard drive. Object storage (S3) holds files. File storage shares across servers.

discovery.text: Each type has different performance, cost, and access patterns. Picking wrong wastes money or hurts speed.

twist.text: Object storage is cheapest but has higher latency. Block is fastest but costs significantly more.

climax.text: Most real applications use all three types together, each for what it does best.

punchline.text: Three storage types, three strengths. Mix them wisely.

quiz.question: Which type of IaaS storage is the cheapest per gigabyte?

details.summary: IaaS storage includes block storage for VM disks, object storage for unstructured data, and file storage for shared access. Each type has different performance, durability, and cost characteristics suited to different workload requirements.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing the wrong storage type leads to performance bottlenecks or excessive costs. Understanding the options ensures data is stored efficiently and accessibly.
takeaways: Block storage provides high-performance VM disk volumes
Object storage offers scalable, durable unstructured storage
File storage enables shared access across multiple instances

faq.question: What is the difference between block and object storage?
faq.answer: Block storage works like a hard drive attached to a VM, supporting random reads and writes at low latency. Object storage stores files as complete objects with metadata, optimized for large-scale reads and writes but not random access within files.

faq.question: Which storage type is cheapest?
faq.answer: Object storage is the cheapest per gigabyte, especially in archive tiers. Block storage costs more due to provisioned IOPS and low latency guarantees. File storage falls in between. Most architectures use a mix based on access patterns.
